problem_type: Resident tool visibility mistaken for surface execution authority
symptom: CI rejects resident delete schema; real creation Composer can delete persisted canvas nodes after confirmation.
direct_cause: B1c made schemas resident while lane before_tool checked approval but never matched renderer mutation port against the consumed Composer target.
class_root: Approval must not expand destructive renderer actions beyond the consumed Composer surface; schema residency cannot substitute for this execution check.
affected_population: Resident creation, canvas and timeline turns, including queued and restored inputs
entry_points: Resident cross-surface canvas and timeline mutations
internal_only_reason: Internal application authority contract; existing pi before_tool block API already used in laneHost, no new external API or format.
invariants: A destructive renderer capability requires the consumed Composer target kind to match its canonical targetKind.
Mismatch or missing target is denied before preparation, approval and execution; schemas remain resident.
Reversible workflows may intentionally cross surfaces, including creation-to-storyboard planning.
generality_proof: Resolve operation-aware capability through the shared catalog and compare destructive renderer capability targetKind for all tool names/providers. Native coding retains its independent unlock. Reversible canvas/document/timeline writes retain their existing domain and approval authority, since creation-to-storyboard intentionally crosses surfaces.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Check consumed input target before domain preparation and approval.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Real HTTP loopback and durable lane tool result plus full canvas equality.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: canvas.delete missing/document/canvas targets; reversible canvas.write, timeline.write, document.write controls
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Missing/document targets deny canvas.delete before lifecycle prepare; canvas target executes. Reversible canvas.write/timeline.write/document.write retain existing cross-surface behavior.

recurrence.reason: Every resident model can call cross-surface mutations now that all schemas remain visible.
same_class_scan: rg not.toContain and toolNames across repository found 3 stale surface/group assertions in two UX walks.
Read laneHost before_tool, laneDesktopTools, laneExtendedDesktopPorts and native assembly; canvas.delete and timeline.write share lifecycle entry.
Legacy agentChatPolicy tests concern the separate semantic MCP/Host alias catalog, not lane residency; retired tool absence checks remain valid.

prevention.invariant: Destructive renderer capability targetKind matches consumed Composer target.
prevention.failure_mode: pi before_tool block returns surface_authority_denied as an error tool result.
prevention.strategy: Derive authority from existing canonical capability execution port and immutable consumed input, never the newest queued draft or visible schema.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove group-unlock-as-visibility assertions and redundant group request fixtures; retain execution approval checks.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency behavior change: use the existing pi before_tool block API and error-result persistence.

migration: No storage migration. Old Composer inputs without target fail closed for destructive renderer writes. Reversible cross-surface workflows and separately authorized non-Composer domain harnesses retain existing behavior.
residual_risks: Authority is scoped to the consumed Composer target; verified domain ports remain responsible for sender, revision, identifiers and current project binding.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The lane execution entrance sees the consumed Composer context and operation-aware canonical tool contract before any lifecycle effect.
